beth-togarmah_239.name: Beth-togarmah
beth-togarmah_239.what: A people and land of the far north, named for Togarmah and known for trading horses and mules.
beth-togarmah_239.today: Exact site unknown; possibly eastern Turkey or Armenia.
key: Beth-togarmah traded horses, war horses, and mules for the wares of Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
Beth-togarmah from the uttermost parts of the north is named among the allies of Gog (Ezekiel 38).

chisloth-tabor_297.name: Chisloth-tabor
chisloth-tabor_297.what: A place on the border of Zebulun near Mount Tabor, on the way toward Daberath.
chisloth-tabor_297.today: Possibly Iksal, near Nazareth in northern Israel.
key: Zebulun's boundary ran east from Sarid to the border of Chisloth-tabor (Joshua 19).
From there the boundary went on to Daberath and up to Japhia (Joshua 19).

gallim_434.name: Gallim
gallim_434.what: A town in Benjamin north of Jerusalem, home of Palti, who was given David's wife Michal.
gallim_434.today: Exact site unknown; north of Jerusalem.
key: Saul gave his daughter Michal, David's wife, to Palti son of Laish, of Gallim (1 Samuel 25).
Isaiah calls the daughter of Gallim to cry aloud as the Assyrian army advances (Isaiah 10).

gob_483.name: Gob
gob_483.what: A battle site where David's men fought the Philistines and killed descendants of the giants.
key: At Gob, Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, a descendant of the giants (2 Samuel 21).
In another battle at Gob, Elhanan of Bethlehem struck down a Philistine giant (2 Samuel 21).

kamon_665.name: Kamon
kamon_665.what: A town in Gilead where Jair, a judge of Israel, was buried.
kamon_665.today: Exact site unknown; in Gilead, in present-day northern Jordan.
key: Jair the Gileadite judged Israel twenty-two years, and his sons had thirty cities in Gilead (Judges 10).
Jair died and was buried in Kamon (Judges 10).

moserah_823.name: Moserah
moserah_823.what: A wilderness camp of Israel, where Deuteronomy records that Aaron died and was buried.
moserah_823.today: Exact site unknown; near the border of Edom.
key: Israel journeyed from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried (Deuteronomy 10).
From there Israel journeyed to Gudgodah and then to Jotbathah (Deuteronomy 10).

second_quarter_1040.name: Second Quarter
second_quarter_1040.what: A newer district of Jerusalem where the prophetess Huldah lived in Josiah's day.
second_quarter_1040.today: Likely the western hill of Jerusalem's Old City.
key: Huldah the prophetess lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter (2 Kings 22).
Chronicles also places Huldah's home in the Second Quarter (2 Chronicles 34).
Zephaniah foretold a wail from the Second Quarter on the day of the LORD (Zephaniah 1).
